paraphrase: Today, in my ocean-hued Lord, I have seen Śrī; I have seen the golden form, the lovely hue of the blazing sun, the golden discus fierce in battle, the spiralled conch in his hand.
speaker: Pēyāḻvār
notes: The vision in the lamplight kindled by Poykai and Pūtam (phn:mutal-alvars-fourth-presence).

paraphrase: At the hill (Tiruvēṅkaṭam) the Lord is seen with matted locks and a tall crown, axe and discus, serpent and golden cord — two forms joined as one.
speaker: Pēyāḻvār
notes: Recalled as Pēyāḻvār's verse on the Lord at Tirumalai bearing marks of both Hari and Hara; ref and exact details low confidence. Śrīvaiṣṇava commentators read it as Śiva abiding as a part of the Lord's body, not as equality.
